about.title: Personal Injury Help in Livermore, California
about.longDescription: Livermore sits at the eastern edge of Alameda County, where I-580 carries commuters in both directions and Isabel Avenue links the freeway to the rest of town. Public records for 2025, the most recent finalized year, list 364 injury collisions in the city, 486 people injured, and 5 traffic deaths. The corridors that show up most often in those counts are I-580 Eastbound, I-580 Westbound, I-580 generally, and Isabel Avenue, and reported crashes tend to peak on Fridays between 5 p.m. and 7 p.m. Behind each number is a person who now has to deal with medical bills, missed work, and an insurance adjuster who calls before the bruises fade. We handle personal injury claims in Livermore and surrounding parts of Alameda County. Our team works on contingency, meaning you owe no attorney fee unless there is a recovery. Whether you were hurt on the freeway, on a city street, or on someone else's property, a conversation with us costs nothing and can help you understand your options before deadlines start to matter.

whyChoose.title: What California Law Means for Your Livermore Claim

items.title: Two years to act, and sometimes far less
items.desc: Most California injury claims must be filed within two years of the injury. If a city, county, or state agency is involved, a claim may need to be presented in as little as six months, so timing matters more than people expect.

items.title: Partial fault does not close the door
items.desc: California follows pure comparative fault. Even if you were partly responsible, you can still pursue compensation; your share of fault reduces the recovery rather than eliminating it.

items.title: No statutory cap on pain-and-suffering damages
items.desc: In ordinary personal injury cases, California places no legal cap on non-economic damages such as pain, suffering, and loss of enjoyment of life. Those losses count, and we can help document them.

items.title: No attorney fee unless there is a recovery
items.desc: We work on contingency. You pay no attorney fee up front, and none at all unless your case results in a recovery.

items.question: Where do crashes in Livermore tend to happen?
items.answer: According to public collision records, the corridors with the highest counts in Livermore are I-580 Eastbound, I-580 Westbound, I-580 generally, and Isabel Avenue. In 2025, the city recorded 364 injury collisions involving 486 injured people and 5 traffic deaths. Reported crashes tend to peak on Fridays between 5 p.m. and 7 p.m. These figures are simply counts from the record and reflect traffic volume, not a judgment about any particular road.

items.question: How long do I have to file an injury claim in California?
items.answer: For most personal injury claims, the deadline is two years from the date of the injury. If your claim is against a government entity, such as a city or Caltrans, you may need to file a formal claim within six months. Because the rules differ by situation, it helps to speak with an attorney early rather than waiting.

items.question: What if I was partly to blame for the crash?
items.answer: California uses pure comparative fault, so being partly responsible does not bar you from recovering. Your compensation is reduced by your percentage of fault. For example, if you are found 20 percent at fault, you could still recover the remaining 80 percent of your damages.

items.question: Do you handle personal injury claims?
items.answer: Yes. We handle personal injury claims in Livermore and surrounding areas of Alameda County. We do not give legal advice beyond your initial consultation; we handle your case directly. There is no cost to contact us for a free case review.

items.question: How does a contingency fee work?
items.answer: We work on contingency, which means we are paid a percentage of any recovery rather than an hourly fee. If there is no recovery, you owe no attorney fee. The specific percentage and terms are explained in the written agreement you sign before any work begins.
